title: Nine Hours of Waiting
subtitle: 出生与诞生 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 出生与诞生（生活与学习·家庭与生命）
meta: 主题语境：出生与诞生（生活与学习·家庭与生命）　|　核心词汇：birth　|　正文 325 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 birth 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 my mother was present at ① a birth that took nine hours, and she said the waiting was the whole of the event. The ② birth, meaning the delivery and not the child, was over by eleven and was described for thirty years; a birth, she said, is the only event that everybody attends and nobody remembers.

Every ③ birth in that family happened in the same room, and the ④ birth in March, meaning the one nobody expected and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever wrote down. A birth, my grandmother said, is nine parts waiting and one part somebody who knows what to do; my mother said the waiting is the part nobody is paid for.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ birth was the whole of the family, meaning the origin and not the delivery. The ⑥ birth, meaning where somebody comes from and not any of that, is the only thing in a village that everybody knows and nobody mentions; a birth, he said, is either something you attend or the only word that means both a delivery and an origin. She said the origin is the part they argue about.

By 1968 the ⑦ birth had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the date. The ⑧ birth of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine hours of waiting and one unwritten March; a birth, she said, is either the delivery in the room or the reason you know which family you belong to. He said the belonging was never in the register.

The ⑨ birth I remember is the one in March, which was written down and then lost. A ⑩ birth, my grandmother said in 1970, is the only event that improves by being unwritten; every birth, she said, is an origin that has agreed to look like a delivery. She said the origin was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 分娩（指那次生产，与孩子相对）
C. 固定搭配：be present at a birth 在场目睹一次分娩
D. n. 分娩（指家里每一次）
E. n. 分娩（指三月那一次）
F. n. 出身；血统（指家族来源）
G. n. 出身（抽象：来自哪里这件事）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a birth that took nine hours
The birth, meaning the delivery and not the child
birth was the whole of the family
The birth, meaning where somebody comes from
the birth had become a line in a register
The birth of the whole thing
A birth, my grandmother said in 1970

answers.why: be present at a birth 意为“在场目睹一次分娩”，1946 年母亲在场目睹了一次持续九小时的分娩。
birth 意为“分娩”，指那次生产而不是孩子，它十一点前结束，却被描述了三十年。
birth 指家里每一次分娩，那个家里每一次都在同一个房间。
birth 指三月那一次（没人料到的那一次），是唯一有人写下来的。
birth 意为“出身、血统”，指家族来源，父亲说 birth 就是那个家族的全部。
birth 为抽象用法，指来自哪里这件事，是村子里人人都知道、却没人提起的东西。
birth 意为“出生、分娩”，到 1968 年这个 birth 成了登记簿里的一行。
birth 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九小时的等待和一个没被记下的三月。
birth 意为“出生”，我记得的是三月那一次，它被写下来，后来又丢了。
birth 为抽象总称，祖母说出生是唯一会因为没被记录而变好的事。

那次分娩，指的是那次生产而不是孩子，十一点前结束，却被描述了三十年。（birth）
那个家里每一次分娩都在同一个房间。（birth）
三月那次分娩，指的是没人料到的那一次，是唯一有人写下来的。（birth）
父亲说 birth 就是那个家族的全部，指的是出身而不是那次分娩。（birth）
1970 年祖母说，出生是唯一会因为没被记录而变好的事。（birth）
